{"id": "783554ec-615e-457e-829f-9390e9188077", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "To diagnose this properly, I'll trace the authorization chain for the Q Apps call specifically — Amazon Q Apps requires extra permissions and resource-level policies beyond what's needed for Q Business chat, so a clean IAM check and Identity Center assignment doesn't rule it out. Common causes for chat-works-but-Apps-403:

- Missing `qapps:*` actions on the Identity Center-provisioned IAM role used for Q Apps calls (separate from the main Q Business chat role)
- The Q Business application's Q Apps capability not enabled at the application level
- A resource policy or app-level permission restricting which users/groups can create or run Q Apps
- An SCP or permission boundary blocking the specific `qapps` namespace while allowing `qbusiness` chat actions

To check the actual configuration, I need a couple of specifics:

1. The Q Business application ID (or name) the user is accessing
2. The affected user's identity — their Identity Center user email or principal ARN

I'll assume this is in your scoped account (012345678901_2, us-east-1) unless you tell me otherwise. Once I have the app ID and user identity, I'll trace through the IAM role, trust policy, resource policies, and SCPs to pinpoint exactly which hop is denying the Q Apps call.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
